source.title: Generalized Derivations and C*-Algebras: Comments and Some Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let H be a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, let L(H) be the algebra of all bounded linear operators on H, and let f be a linear functional on L(H). Define alpha(f) to be the set of all pairs (A, B) in L(H) x L(H) such that f(AX) = f(XB) for every X in L(H). Characterize the conditions under which alpha(f), with the natural pair operations and adjoint inherited from L(H) x L(H), is a C*-algebra.

evidence.quote: Question 3.1. Does α(f) = {(A, B) ∈L(H)×L(H) : f(AX) = f(XB), ∀X ∈ L(H)} is a C⋆- algebra?
Question 4.1. For which A, B ∈L(H), α(f) is a C⋆-algebra ?

accepted.question_text: Let H be a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space and let L(H) be the algebra of all bounded linear operators on H. For A, B in L(H), define the generalized derivation delta_A,B on L(H) by delta_A,B(X) = AX - XB, and let R(delta_A,B) be its range. Call the pair (A, B) generalized finite when ||I - (AX - XB)|| >= 1 for every X in L(H). If there exists a normal, self-adjoint linear functional f on L(H) such that f(Y) = 0 for every Y in R(delta_A,B), must the pair (A, B) be generalized finite?

evidence.quote: Such operators are called generalized finite operators.
Question 4.2. Let A, B ∈L(H). If there is a linear form f ∈L(H)′, which is normal, self-adjoint and f(R(δA,B)) = 0. Does the pair (A, B) generalized finite ?

needs_review.question_text_raw: Let A, B ∈ L(H). Does the following statements equivalent: (1) (A, B) is generalized finite. (2) ρ = [C⋆(A, B), L(H) × L(H)] is not norm dense (3) The vector space generated by (R(δA,B) ∪ R(δA⋆,B⋆)) is not norm dense?

evidence.quote: Question 4.3. Let A, B ∈L(H). Does the following statements equivalent:
(2) ρ = [C⋆(A, B), L(H) × L(H)] is not norm dense
